britannica-1911-kivu:
Kivu is a large lake in the rift valley of central Africa. The 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica sets it north of Tanganyika, with the Rusizi river linking them. Volcanic peaks north of the lake cut it off from the Nile basin. Its shores are high and broken, with cliffs of volcanic rock.

The lake is deep and holds many fish but no crocodiles or hippos. A large island, Kwijwi, lies south west of its center point. Falls on the Rusizi drop two thousand feet toward Tanganyika below. Count von Götzen first visited the lake for Europe in 1894. Belgium and Germany settled rival claims to its shores in 1910.
